reviewType: AI source and canonical owner-scope comparison

sourceEvidence.sourceSentence: The support team works around the clock.
sourceEvidence.sourceMeaning: Continuously, day and night; a fixed time expression.
sourceEvidence.canonicalMeaning: Oversight maintained throughout the day and night.

primaryLanguageSources.title: Cambridge Dictionary: round/around the clock
primaryLanguageSources.evidence: Defines the unhyphenated idiom as all day and all night and shows work around the clock as verb modification, alongside round-the-clock nursing as noun modification.

primaryLanguageSources.title: Cambridge Dictionary: round-the-clock
primaryLanguageSources.evidence: Labels the hyphenated phrase an adjective before a noun and exemplifies round-the-clock care.

comparison.sharedSense: Both communicate day-and-night continuity; grammar alone does not create a different time meaning.
comparison.distinctConstruction: Source 2736 uses unhyphenated around the clock adverbially after works and can modify work, operate, update or similar actions. Canonical 1343 fixes the attributive phrase round-the-clock supervision and teaches oversight of a particular object/person.
comparison.differentLearnerDecision: The new learner applies an adverbial time claim to ongoing work and keeps effort separate from a finished result. Canonical 1343 checks whether planned supervision covers overnight hours, handovers and permission before naming staff.
comparison.patternEvidence: The proposed detector matches the complete source example and does not match the canonical example; the canonical detector matches its own example and does not match source 2736. This is a construction check, not proof of semantic independence.

sevenStepFeasibility: Listening: interpret day-and-night repair effort with rotating crews, without claiming a completed repair.
Four-valid reply: report overlapping day/night work on a temporary software fix while testing remains open.
Scene: choose a truthful description of road crews working across day and night while the road stays closed.
Contrast: distinguish full twenty-four-hour coverage from a long day with an overnight gap or a single night shift.
Dialogue: reject an around-the-clock claim when work stops between 01:00 and 08:00, while acknowledging late work.
Speaking: say that rotating restoration teams continue working while some recordings remain unrecovered.
Writing: describe a new community-site update task with assigned early/afternoon/overnight shifts, noting that some notices still require verification.
decision: Provisional separate lesson is teachable as an adverbial construction and operational-reporting decision despite shared continuous-time semantics; retain source 2736's existing proposed-new-lesson editorial decision. Require an independent editorial review and human owner-scope sign-off before selection. No automatic alias or release is justified.
